# Connected affine groups are generated by their Cartan subgroups

Worker 1342.

`Langlands.GroupScheme.CartanGenerationStatement.{u}` states the
infinite-field affine case of Milne's Theorem 17.91. For every infinite
field `k : Type u` and actual group scheme `G` over `Spec k` that is smooth,
affine and connected, every actual closed subgroup `i : H ⟶ G` containing
all Cartan subgroups has `SubgroupFunctor.range i = ⊤`.

The containment premise quantifies over every group scheme `C` and every
homomorphism `c : C ⟶ G` satisfying the published predicate
`IsCartanSubgroup c`. Such a `c` is a closed representative of the centralizer
of some maximal torus of `G`. Containment is `FactorsThrough c.hom.hom i`:
there is an actual morphism of schemes over `Spec k` from `C.X` to `H.X`
whose composite with `i` is `c`. The competitor `H` is not required to be
smooth, reduced, connected, or itself a Cartan subgroup.

The conclusion is equality of subgroup functors on every scheme over
`Spec k`, including nonaffine and nonreduced test schemes. For a closed
embedding this is equivalent to the embedding being an isomorphism: apply
the range equality on the test scheme `G.X` to its identity point to obtain
a right inverse, and use monicity for the other inverse equation. Thus the
conclusion says exactly that no proper algebraic subgroup contains all
Cartan subgroups, rather than only asserting generation on `k`-points.

## Original source and conventions

The source is J. S. Milne, *Algebraic Groups* (2017), Theorem 17.91, printed
p.381 (PDF p.397), registered as `milne-2017-algebraic-groups`, SHA256
`899b0f44f3c3ccfbaf5ed1cf9c180be7a8016b1c0e9709ca0c206304e5bd1cd0`.
It states that every connected group variety is generated by its Cartan
subgroups. Its proof treats infinite fields, then refers the finite-field
case to Borel and Springer. The Lean statement retains only the
infinite-field affine case needed by the rational-point density project.
It makes no assertion about finite fields or nonaffine groups.

The source's Cartan convention is Definition 17.43, printed p.364
(PDF p.380): the centralizer of a maximal torus. This is the convention in
`Langlands.GroupScheme.Cartan.Basic`. In the present smooth connected affine
setting it has the actual scheme-theoretic meaning used in the source;
its extension to arbitrary ambient group schemes is explained in that
module's Markdown. Smoothness implies local finite presentation, and
affineness implies quasi-compactness, so the hypotheses on `G` give a
connected affine group variety of finite type over `k`.

Generation is the algebraic-subgroup minimality of Proposition 2.51,
printed p.56 (PDF p.72). For closed embeddings its factorization formulation
agrees with the source's containment formulation. No assertion that the
abstract group `G(k)` is generated by Cartan rational points is made.

The complete registered errata snapshot
`milne-2017-algebraic-groups-errata-2026-11-02`, SHA256
`a0c3a10dc376e1c9bd1de05b33beaf7d54e5f1ea7b408d594cfd70231a7ba0cf`,
was read. It has no correction to 2.51, 17.43 or 17.91. The correction to
Example 17.42 on the preceding source page does not change these statements.

## Proof and consumer boundary

This module records a proposition and supplies no proof. Milne's proof uses
nilpotent-group structure (16.47), spanning by Lie algebras of connected
centralizers of noncentral semisimple Lie elements (17.79), and maximality
of their maximal tori in `G` (17.90), followed by dimension induction.
These structural inputs are not assumed by the Lean proposition or proved
here. A proof may use a different valid route with every input discharged.

The statement imposes no reductivity, perfection, splitting, positive-rank
or positive-dimension hypothesis. In the reductive density project,
`MaximalTorusCentralizerStatement` separately identifies Cartan subgroups
with maximal tori. The generic finite-subfamily argument then supplies
finiteness. Neither that identification, finite torus generation, nor
rational-point density follows from this statement file alone.
